memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So the slave drivers and the overseers went out and said to the people, "This is what Pharaoh says: 'I will not give you any more straw. Go and get your own straw wherever you can find it, but your work will not be reduced at all.'" So the people scattered all over Egypt to gather stubble to use for straw." - Exodus 5:10-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The picture in verse 12 is heartbreaking. A whole nation scattered across Egypt, scrabbling in fields for stubble — the leftover bits of straw — because the proper straw has been withdrawn.

They were already exhausted. Now they must do a second full job before they can begin the first.

Many people live here. Working two jobs to cover one set of bills. Caring for children and ageing parents at the same time. Studying at night after working all day. Scattered, scavenging, never enough hours.

Scripture does not pretend this is fine. It records it as oppression, and God will act against it. Our God notices unjust systems and He notices tired people. He commanded Israel later to pay a worker before sunset because He knew what it was to be poor and waiting.

If you are scattered and scavenging today, know this: God sees the stubble in your hands. He has not mistaken your exhaustion for weakness of faith.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I running on empty, and have I told God honestly?
2. Is there someone around me carrying a double burden whom I could help?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You see how tired I am and how far I have had to stretch. Give me strength for today and mercy for the people around me. Amen.
